title: SCALING READS
subtitle: Most systems read far more than they write. Make the common read cheap, and the database only sees what the cache can't answer.
footer: Theory: DDIA ch 5 Replication · DDIA ch 6 Partitioning

items: The same items are read over and over (popularity is skewed).
A read path misses its latency target, or the calculated read QPS exceeds what one database serves (~10–50k/s).
One database serves every read. At ~10k+ reads/sec it becomes the bottleneck.
Cache-aside: check Redis; on a miss, read the DB and populate the cache with a TTL. A hit takes <1ms vs ~5–50ms from the DB.
Read replicas spread the remaining reads (expect replication lag, DDIA Ch 5).
CDN serves static and shared responses from the edge, so origin never sees them.
Is the response the same for many users? Put a CDN in front.
Is it per-user but read often? Cache-aside in Redis with a TTL.
Still too much load on the primary? Add read replicas and accept replication lag.
Is one key extremely hot? Replicate the key or add a short-lived local cache.
Which reads must never be stale? Send those to the primary.

blocks.text: "Reads outnumber writes about 100 to 1 and popularity is skewed, so a cache-aside Redis layer should absorb most reads. The rest go to replicas; only checkout reads the primary."

items: Sharding the database before trying a cache and replicas.
Caching data that must be exact (stock at checkout, balances).
Forgetting cache stampedes on hot keys.

blocks.text: Used in: URL shortener (Bitly), Rate limiter, Business discovery (Yelp), News feed (Facebook), News aggregator (Google News), Local delivery (Gopuff), Dating app (Tinder), Distributed cache, Post search (Facebook), Price tracker (CamelCamelCamel), Ticketmaster, Video platform (YouTube), Photo sharing (Instagram)
